smell_validity.evidence: Both reporting and traversal layers re-read the run's mode fields and page through the record's bytes to decide what the data itself owns; the record carries no interpreting methods and the report holds the run purely to read it. Duplicated rule copies must stay in agreement across layers, so misplaced ownership and its divergence cost are unmistakable.

maintenance_impact.evidence: The injection multiplied each rule the monolith held once: reporting-mode dispatch, fragment options and the plain-output fallback now exist as private copies in two layers that must be edited in step. Divergence silently splits stdin from named-file behavior and the tally from exit-status accounting; restoring ownership makes those invariants structural.

development_plausibility.evidence: This is the authentic halfway refactor: the split into run, record, reporting and traversal objects mirrors how Go tools of this size actually grow, keeping byte-identical behavior and gofmt-style file organization. The leftover reach-through reads like a compromise left after useful work, not task scaffolding; no filler appears.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: The four complaints point at the exact envy sites, and the rules pin completion: every CLI observation (exit 2 cases, walk continuity, diff headers, stdin fragment) is named literally, partial fixes are excluded ('both layers, more than one place each'; scaffolding must not survive), and the flag surface bounds redesign. Wrong direction, incomplete cleanup and drift are all decisively precluded.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Four distinct purposes need different code-supported decisions: relocating mode interpretation to the run's owner, moving record work (change detection, diff, self-format) onto the record, splitting diagnostics from the failure tally, and reusing the run's existing option derivation on the stdin path. Each touches a different method surface, input or caller set.

localization_burden.evidence: The prompt names both layers, the stdin path and the handle, but classifying each site still requires combining components: recognizing the stdin path's rule copies means comparing them against the run's existing derivation and the reporting layer's twin branch. No alias, callback or configuration chase is required.

repair_coordination.evidence: Two rules collide: handing mode verdicts to the run owner forces the reporting and stdin presentation seams to move together (fix one layer only and stdin drifts from named files on future mode changes), while removing the report's run handle re-plumbs the shared failure tally across every reporting call site that sets exit code 2.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: Mechanically extracting record questions (changed?, self-format) fully covers only the named-file formatting site of roughly six; every other site needs an ownership decision. Direct alternatives were checked: reusing the run's existing option derivation, delegating stdin presentation, and getter-style parameterization each cover one site or none, differing in inputs, written targets or streams.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Plausible wrong edits compile and pass healthy runs: dropping one tally increment while re-plumbing problem reporting yields exit 0 instead of 2, and a walk callback that stops on error skips later files; both surface only in special states (failing inputs, bad files mid-directory). No test or execution evidence shows these paths checked.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
